sections.label: Restructuring IDA and MDA
sections.summary: In January, the speaker announced IDA and MDA will be restructured into IMDA and GovTech.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In January this year, I announced that we will restructure the Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore (IDA) and the Media Development Authority of Singapore (MDA) into two new organisations ‒ the Info-communications Media Development Authority, or IMDA for short, and the Government Technology Agency, or GovTech for short.

sections.label: IDA telecommunications market liberalisation
sections.summary: IDA fully liberalised Singapore's telecommunications market in 2000, two years early, and ensured nationwide fibre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: IDA fully liberalised Singapore's telecommunications market in 2000, two years ahead of schedule, and ensured that we are the only country in the world that has nationwide fibre in our homes and businesses.

sections.label: Converged infocomm media regulator
sections.summary: The process confirmed the view that the time is right to set up a converged infocomm media developer and regulator.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The process has confirmed our view that the time is right to set up a converged infocomm media developer and regulator.

sections.label: Bill establishing IMDA
sections.summary: The Bill before the House will legally establish IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Bill before this House will legally establish IMDA.

sections.label: Sector legislation and competition provisions
sections.summary: Subject-specific legislation for telecommunications, media and postal sectors will continue under IMDA, with MDA Act competition provisions carried into Part 7.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: With the formation of IMDA, subject-specific legislation for the telecommunications, media and postal sectors will continue and will be implemented by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For expediency, the market competition provisions in the MDA Act will be carried forward into Part 7 of the IMDA Bill as an interim measure.

sections.label: Commission unit under IMDA
sections.summary: When IMDA is formed, the Commission will be a unit under IMDA to enforce private sector data protection regulation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: When IMDA is formed, the Commission will be a unit under IMDA to enforce data protection regulation in the private sector.

sections.label: IMDA powers not expanded
sections.summary: IMDA will have no additional functions and powers beyond those IDA and MDA currently have.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: IMDA will not have any additional functions and powers beyond what IDA and MDA currently have.

sections.label: IMDA Bill parts and restructuring
sections.summary: Parts 3 to 6 cover IMDA's Board, employees and finances, Part 8 enforcement powers, Parts 9 and 10 transfers and repeals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Parts 3 to 6 are on matters regarding IMDA's Board members, their decision-making procedures, IMDA's own employees and its financial provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These provisions were ported over from the MDA Act and are essential to give IMDA the legislative powers to intervene in competition-related matters that have an impact on the industry and consumers, including mergers and consolidations that involve media companies, and potential abuse of market powers by dominant media companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Part 8 of the Bill sets out the administration and enforcement powers of IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These apply to offences under the IMDA Bill and do not replace the enforcement powers that are in IMDA's subject-specific legislation, like the Telecommunications Act and the Broadcasting Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Parts 9 and 10 contain provisions that transfer the relevant undertakings and personnel to IMDA, to repeal the IDA and MDA Acts and provide for saving and transitional arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The restructuring of IDA and MDA is both relevant and timely and will support the development of the Infocomm Media 2025 plan.

sections.label: Companies deal with one agency
sections.summary: Under IMDA, companies need only work with one agency guided by the converged policy framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the newly formed IMDA though, these companies need only to work with one agency guided by the converged policy framework.

sections.label: Review of sports content competition
sections.summary: A request is made for IMDA to review possible market failure or lack of competition in expensive exclusive sports content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this respect, I would also like to ask IMDA to review the possible market failure or issues with lack of competition which results in Singaporeans being taken hostage to pay for expensive, exclusive sports content.

sections.label: IMDA aims and priorities
sections.summary: IMDA aims to equip Singaporeans with digital skills and lists priorities including growing the infocomm media sector and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To begin with, IMDA aims to equip Singaporeans with the skills to thrive in a digital future and drive the domestic economy by promoting digital connectivity and creativity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is important to note that in terms of its industry development focus, the priorities of IMDA are to grow the infocomm media sector, foster a stronger culture of creating and building, building a future-ready Singapore Core for infocomm and media, strengthening Singapore's connectivity and harnessing data as a competitive advantage.

sections.label: Single agency benefit and clarity
sections.summary: Service providers can deal with a single agency, but IMDA's overall functions, including media content regulation, need clearer explanation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One clear benefit is that service providers and companies that previously dealt with IDA and MDA separately can now deal with a single agency only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the overall functions of IMDA need to be explained more clearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, will it supervise the regulation of media content and will changes be made to the regulations since the same content can be published on various platforms?

sections.label: Manpower plans through IMDA
sections.summary: The passage asks to be told of plans to develop suitable manpower and strategies through IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In terms of expertise and talent, it is also important to let us know about the plans to develop suitable manpower and the strategies that will be adopted, through IMDA.

sections.label: Regulating converged infocomm media sector
sections.summary: The authority will regulate a converged infocomm media sector and safeguard consumer interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The authority will regulate a converged infocomm media sector and safeguard the interests of consumers as well.

sections.label: Funding for local content creators
sections.summary: The passage seeks clarification on whether the funding model for local content initiatives would differ under the merged entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, in terms of support for local content creators and to promote Singapore as a place to create content, I would like to seek clarification on whether the funding model for these initiatives Page: 118 would be different under the merged and enlarged entity as opposed to when MDA was a separate agency.

sections.label: Rio Olympics broadcast rights impasse
sections.summary: Singaporeans almost missed Joseph Schooling's first Olympic gold live had the Rio Olympics broadcast rights impasse not been resolved last minute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans almost missed out watching history being made "live" from Rio de Janeiro last Saturday, when Joseph Schooling won the first-ever Olympic gold medal for the country, had the impasse in the broadcast rights for the Rio Olympics not been resolved at the very last minute.

sections.label: IMDA, GovTech restructuring and PPPs
sections.summary: The passage urges IMDA to facilitate more PPPs for services and content, and supports IDA and MDA being reorganised as IMDA and GovTech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can it not do something for events that happen only once in every four years, and of which Singaporean athletes are participating, and winning as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge IMDA to look into facilitating more PPPs in bringing services and contents that may not attract viable commercial interests but may bring immeasurable benefits to the nation as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, IDA and MDA will be re-organised as IMDA and GovTech, and I support this restructuring which aligns with the development of the environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IMDA will serve the public at large and the private sector, while the GovTech will focus on the public sector.

sections.label: Singapore's global IT rankings
sections.summary: The Global Information Technology Report 2016 ranks Singapore's e-Government services second, business-to-consumer Internet use 24th and innovation capacity 19th.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Global Information Technology Report 2016, our e-Government services rank No 2 globally, but we only rank 24 in business-to-consumer Internet use, with capacity for innovation ranking 19.

sections.label: IMDA coordinating infocommunications sectors
sections.summary: Restructuring agencies and having IMDA coordinate infocommunications for public and private sectors could improve Singapore's ICT applications for business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through restructuring the Government agencies, getting IMDA to coordinate the infocommunications for the public and private sectors and digital media applications, this could hopefully be an instrumental change to improve Singapore's overall information and communications (ICT) applications for business.

sections.label: MDA function wording omission
sections.summary: MDA's Act clause 11(b) says it encourages, promotes and facilitates the industry, but the new Bill's clause 5(1) omits 'to encourage'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MDA has recognised this and, as such, its functions, as stipulated in its Act, chapter 172, clause 11(b) states that it is to encourage, promote and facilitate the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask this because I noted that the new Bill states in clause 5(1) that the authority's function includes, I quote, "to promote the efficiency, competitiveness (including internationally) and the development of its information, communications and media industry in Singapore".

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The omission of the term "to encourage" differs from MDA's stated function.

sections.label: Arts Entertainment Licence short notice
sections.summary: An Arts Entertainment Licence application was submitted in time, but organisers were told three days before the show to remove objectionable photographs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The application for an Arts Entertainment Licence was submitted within the application period and yet it was only three days prior to the show that the organisers were told to remove a number of photographs found to be objectionable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clearly, a three-day lead time gave little room for negotiation and appeal.

sections.label: Media Convergence Review panel and IMDA
sections.summary: MICA appointed the Media Convergence Review panel in early 2012; by 2016 convergence intensified, making IMDA's setting up timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, in early 2012, the then Ministry of Information, Communications and the Arts, or MICA, appointed the Media Convergence Review panel to study how a converged media space would impact Singapore as a whole and the type of regulatory framework that would be best suited in the new converged media space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Four years later, in 2016, this convergence has only intensified, and the setting up of IMDA is thus timely as the proliferation of Internet-enabled devices and the digitisation of media have enabled content to be consumed in novel and innovative ways.

sections.label: Pokemon Go augmented reality regulation
sections.summary: With Pokemon Go a global hit, more developers may create augmented reality content, so IMDA is asked about extending its regulatory framework to mobile apps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With Pokemon Go! being a massive global hit now, more app developers will emulate the likeness of that app and create more digital content that uses what we call augmented reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, would IMDA consider extending its regulatory framework to cover these mobile apps so that we could avoid the possible downsides of some of these apps?

sections.label: MCI and MOE career tracks
sections.summary: Citing Acting Minister Ong Ye Kung on competencies and skills, the speaker hopes MCI works with MOE to combine career paths and compensation in PSEIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: During the earlier debate on the SkillsFuture Singapore Agency Bill, Acting Minister Ong Ye Kung talked about how competencies and skills matter and how organisations should hire based on competencies and skills, and not just academic results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I hope therefore, that MCI can work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to expedite the process of combining the career paths and compensation packages of the two tracks in these PSEIs to facilitate the hiring of talented and capable infocomm and media professionals who actually display competencies and skills.

sections.label: MDA age check firewalls
sections.summary: MDA introduced a regulation requiring online content providers to provide age check firewalls for R21 content, matching pay television rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Early last month, MDA introduced a new regulation which said that online content providers – the likes of Netflix and others like Viu, which offers Korean content, and even Singapore's very own Toggle, just to name a few – must provide age check firewalls for R21 content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This marks a watershed in media regulations in Singapore as it acknowledges the fact that, in this new digital world, you cannot have blanket censorship laws to govern the on-demand world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The response of MDA was a measured one in that it not only allowed Netflix to offer the programmes that were most sought after, but also created a level playing field with the rest of the pay television market by instituting the same age check firewalls that it already has for R21 content on our pay platforms like Starhub and Singtel MIO.

sections.label: Watching Schooling and Joseph
sections.summary: The speaker watched Schooling race Michael Phelps and Joseph win Singapore's first Olympic Gold, including on Mediacorp's Toggle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last week, the family and I stayed up to watch Schooling go head-to-head against Michael Phelps in the heats of the 100-metre Butterfly, and I was watching him again on Mediacorp's Toggle in the office when he clocked the fastest time in the semi-finals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also watched Joseph make history in the pool by claiming our first-ever Olympic Gold!

sections.label: Missed Olympic broadcast moments
sections.summary: The speaker says a deal to broadcast the Olympics in Singapore was reached only at the eleventh hour after almost three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We would have missed seeing a Singaporean beat the world's best swimmer and greatest Olympian of all time, missed seeing him touch the wall for a new Olympic record, missed seeing him receive the Gold medal, missed seeing our flag flying high, ahead of others, at the world's greatest sporting games, and missed hearing our National Anthem being played for the first time in Olympic history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is extremely puzzling to me that a deal to broadcast the Olympics in Singapore could not be reached over almost a three-year period, and this was achieved only at the eleventh hour.

sections.label: MDA and Olympics impasse
sections.summary: The speaker asks why MDA did not step in during the almost three-year impasse between negotiating parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What if we had missed out on arguably Singapore's most significant 50 seconds of sporting history as it unfolded?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, when there was almost a three-year impasse between the negotiating parties, why did MDA not step in in the interest of the nation?

sections.label: Safeguards and IMDA funding
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill must include safeguards and suggests IMDA fund Olympic telecast rights from PSB funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If Singapore broadcasters will not work together in the spirit of national interest, then this Bill must include safeguards to ensure that this never happens again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, a strong case can be made for the Olympic Games' telecast rights in Singapore to be funded by IMDA as part of the PSB funds that are disbursed annually.

sections.label: Mediacorp outsourcing public service projects
sections.summary: Mediacorp outsources 40% of public service-funded projects to independent production companies in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our national free-to-air broadcaster, Mediacorp, today outsources 40% of public service-funded projects to independent production companies in the private sector.

sections.label: Freelancer support and insurance issues
sections.summary: The Attach-and-Train programme subsidises 70% of freelancers' pay for six months, but insurance coverage remains a serious issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Programmes, such as the Attach-and-Train programme, which subsidises employers to pay 70% of freelancers' pay for six months, have helped provide some stability to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are still, however, serious issues confronting the community, such as insurance coverage for freelancers.

sections.label: Media freelancers' guild issues
sections.summary: A media freelancers' guild would address insurance, talent standards, payment, pipelines and structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A media freelancers' guild would address issues, such as insurance, talent standards, payment, pipelines and structure.

sections.label: DBS phishing email malware case
sections.summary: A June phishing email pretending to be from DBS carried malware that infected devices and stole login and authorisation details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A case emerged in June this year involving a phishing email which pretended to be sent from the Development Bank of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When the attached zip file was opened, the malware it contains would immediately infect the customer's computer or device and steal its login and authorisation details.

sections.label: New agency personal data protection
sections.summary: The question asks what further efforts the new agency will put in place to protect personal data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, could the Minister clarify what further efforts will be put in place by the new agency with regard to the protection of personal data?

sections.label: IMDA dual role and public consultation
sections.summary: The question asks how the authority will decide and whether more public consultations can be held, noting IMDA's dual development and regulation roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the authority will make these decisions and whether more public consultations can be conducted to ensure we better understand the interest of the general public?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, Mr Darryl David asked about the dual role of IMDA in terms of infocomm media industry development and regulation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: There can be significant synergies when a single organisation undertakes both regulation and industry development roles, as many of the policy trade-offs and discussions can take place concurrently.

sections.label: Freelancer insurance in PSB productions
sections.summary: MDA worked with the Association of Independent Producers to include freelancers' insurance as a qualifying cost item in PSB-funded productions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I echo Mr Ganesh Rajaram's comments that freelancers are very important in the media industry.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: That is why MDA has been with the Association of Independent Producers to encourage the adoption of industry best practices, such as including freelancers' insurance as a qualifying cost item in all PSB-funded productions in MDA's master agreement with Mediacorp.

sections.label: PSB funding for independent producers
sections.summary: Since 2013, some PSB funding has been set aside for independent producers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since 2013, we have set aside some PSB funding for independent producers.

sections.label: IDA ICT Skills Framework consultation
sections.summary: Earlier this month, IDA launched an industry consultation for its first draft of the ICT Skills Framework under TeSA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, earlier this month, IDA launched an industry consultation for its first draft of the ICT Skills Framework under TeSA.

sections.label: Regulatory framework guiding principles
sections.summary: The regulatory framework in this area has always been guided by three fundamental principles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Our regulatory framework in this area has always been guided by three fundamental principles: protect the young while providing more choices for adults; reflect community values and support racial and religious harmony; and safeguard national and public interest.

sections.label: MDA concerns over photography exhibition
sections.summary: MDA informed the organiser of its concerns about the exhibition's photographs of members of a terrorist-linked organisation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the photography exhibition "I Know Why The Rebel Sings", MDA informed the organiser of its concerns as soon as MDA determined, after consultation, that the exhibition contained photographs of members from a terrorist-linked organisation who had committed acts of violence to further their cause, such as suicide bombing.

sections.label: Deal for live Olympics coverage
sections.summary: The parties eventually reached a deal allowing Singaporeans to watch the Olympics live and celebrate Joseph Schooling's achievement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I am glad that, in the end, the parties eventually reached a deal that allowed Singaporeans to watch the Olympics "live", cheer our Team Singapore athletes on, and join in celebrating Joseph Schooling's historic achievement.

sections.label: IMDA working with other agencies
sections.summary: IMDA will work with agencies including GovTech to help businesses leverage infocomm media technologies to transform.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In addition, IMDA will also work with other agencies, including GovTech, to help businesses better leverage infocomm media technologies to transform – and I thank Mr Thomas Chua for raising this point.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am confident that IMDA will be a forward-looking organisation that will help Singapore and Singaporeans seize the exciting opportunities in the infocomm media sector through dynamic industry and manpower development initiatives, while safeguarding the interests of consumers and fostering pro-enterprise regulations.      .
